title: A shared budget. Your own boundaries.
description: A budget for two with chosen shared categories and private entries. Both see the updates, understand the balance and decide which information the partner can see.

blocks.text: People can keep separate accounts and still run a shared spending plan. A joint budget requires an agreement about which amounts and transactions each can see. The roles differ from couple to couple and are not set by gender or by the size of an income.

quote.text: My wife and I use Monarch to manage expenses, track savings and investments across multiple accounts. Since we do not combine accounts, monarch allows for both us to have a consolidated view of our household finances.

blocks.text: Create a shared part of the budget and let each person choose what data goes into it. For a shared transaction, show who made the change. Discuss large expenses and limits by agreed rules, without opening up every personal purchase automatically.

Go through one shared goal and one unexpected expense with both people. Do they understand the available money and the visibility of the records the same way? If explaining a number requires access to the whole personal history, the boundaries of shared tracking haven’t been thought through yet.
